records.claim: The decay interval parameter defines the number of decoded instructions after which a digest is invalidated.
records.quote: Consequently, RUNLTS invalidates each digest after 256 subsequent instructions have been decoded, ensuring that only up-to-date information influences future predictions.
records.why: Establishes that digest invalidation is governed by a decay period of 256 subsequent decoded instructions.

records.claim: The decay_step algorithm triggers at instruction decode time and is evaluated per decoded instruction.
records.quote: Consequently, RUNLTS invalidates each digest after 256 subsequent instructions have been decoded, ensuring that only up-to-date information influences future predictions.
records.why: Because decay is counted in terms of decoded instructions, the decay step is evaluated on each decoded instruction.

records.claim: For each decoded instruction, the decay counter of each valid register entry is decremented, and the valid bit is cleared when the counter reaches zero.
records.quote: Consequently, RUNLTS invalidates each digest after 256 subsequent instructions have been decoded, ensuring that only up-to-date information influences future predictions.
records.why: Specifies that digest validity expires after 256 decoded instructions, implemented via decrementing the per-entry decay counter to zero.

records.claim: Digest invalidation prevents stale digests beyond 256 decoded instructions from biasing branch predictions.

records.why: Verbatim justifies the 256-instruction decay by noting stale digests degrade prediction accuracy and must not influence future predictions.
